name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{y}},\,y(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Use the tangent line approximation of $y(x)$ at $x=\frac{1}{2}$ to approximate $y(\frac{3}{4}).$ Do not round the answer.

$y(\frac{3}{4})≈$  
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation to $y(x)$ at the point $a=\frac{1}{2}$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =y(a)+{y}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =y(\frac{1}{2})+{y}^{′}(\frac{1}{2})(x-\frac{1}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

From the initial condition, we know that $y(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{1}{4}.$ We also know that ${y}^{′}(x)=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{y}},$ so

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\frac{1}{2}) & =-\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}}} \\  & =-\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting our values for $y(\frac{1}{2})$ and ${y}^{′}(\frac{1}{2})$ into our expression for $L(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =y(\frac{1}{2})+{y}^{′}(\frac{1}{2})(x-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+(-1)(x-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}-x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can approximate $y(\frac{3}{4})$ using $L(\frac{3}{4}).$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}y(\frac{3}{4}) & ≈L(\frac{3}{4}) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}-\frac{3}{4} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent line approximation to y(x) at the point a=12 is given by L(x)=y(a)+y′(a)(x−a)=y(12)+y′(12)(x−12).

From the initial condition, we know that y(12)=14. We also know that y′(x)=−xy, so y′(12)=−(12)14=−(12)(12)=−1.

Substituting our values for y(12) and y′(12) into our expression for L(x) gives L(x)=y(12)+y′(12)(x−12)=14+(−1)(x−12)=34−x.

Finally, we can approximate y(34) using L(34). We get y(34)≈L(34)=34−34=0.
